questions: Trace job ownership, fingerprints, restart requests and terminal evidence pinning.
Measure resume without model redispatch and safe cancellation of tracked descendants.
decision: Make supervised validation jobs idempotent, generation-bound state machines that resume validation without redispatching the implementation model and reconcile uncertain job outcomes before restart.
code_observations: jobctl tracks job status, ownership, process identity, waiting and cancellation separately from model execution.
run_isolated can resume validation after a worker checkpoint, avoiding another model call when only a mapped job remains.
implementation_steps: Pin each job request to validation ID, source/map/command digest and execution identity. A stale succeeded job cannot satisfy a new acceptance state.
Make start/resume idempotent for an existing live matching job and refuse ambiguous ownership. Do not relaunch merely because a status wait returned75.
Persist bounded terminal receipts before releasing ownership, and define recovery after process loss between completion and receipt writing.
Preserve job evidence on ordinary interruption. Explicit cancellation/reset must stop owned descendants before removing controls.
Keep external side effects outside assumed exactly-once guarantees; expose an idempotency key or a reconciliation requirement for commands that cannot safely repeat.
Bind job evidence to task, attempt, command and source/map generation; stale success cannot satisfy acceptance.
Test the launch-before-record crash window and reconcile ownership before redispatch.
Resume pending validation from its implementation checkpoint without invoking the model again.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Two start requests for the same pinned live job create only one process.
A completed validation checkpoint resumes without redispatching the model.
A succeeded job with changed source/map/command is rejected as stale.
Wait timeout leaves the live job intact and returns its state, not a false failure.
Crash/cancel tests preserve receipts or explicitly report uncertainty rather than inventing completion.
Crash after process launch does not produce a second writer during recovery.
A successful receipt with an outdated map/input digest is rejected.
Validation-only resume performs zero model dispatches.
Cleanup cannot delete state while an owned job termination remains uncertain.

alternatives.title: Rerun implementation after every interruption
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy control flow; Duplicates edits and model cost. Reject

alternatives.title: Treat a detached PID as durable state
alternatives.tradeoff: Minimal metadata; PID reuse and lost outcomes. Reject

alternatives.title: Journaled job identity plus reconciliation
alternatives.tradeoff: Resumable and cost-efficient; Requires crash-window tests. Recommended

alternatives.title: External workflow database for every job
alternatives.disposition: Defer until multi-host scale requires it
alternatives.tradeoff: Strong centralized durability; Operational dependency disproportionate here. Defer until multi-host scale requires it

cost_model: Avoid a full model retry when only validation remains; compare recovery work, repeated tests and model calls per interruption scenario.
unverified: Arbitrary shell commands cannot be made exactly-once merely by saving a JSON job record. External services need their own idempotency/reconciliation contract.
Local checkpoint tests cannot establish multi-host exactly-once semantics. Remote coordination is explicitly outside the portable single-host implementation.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Keep supervised jobs as durable owned executions with pinned results; distinguish resuming observation from launching the same side effect again.
revision_delta: The revision adds the crash window between process launch and receipt persistence, map-generation binding and the difference between detached job liveness and validated success.
decision_analysis: A durable job is not just a subprocess launched with a detached flag. Its record should bind job id, task/attempt, command, working directory, input/map digest and owned process identity. A receipt from an older command or changed source cannot satisfy the current task even when it reports exit zero.

Launching a process and writing metadata are not one atomic transaction. If the host crashes between those operations, recovery must reconcile the owned process or an idempotency marker before launching a duplicate. Never promise exactly-once execution merely because a JSON file was written atomically.

An implementation report may be ready while long validation remains running. Persist that checkpoint so resume waits for or revalidates the same job instead of spending another model call to reimplement the feature. A succeeded job still needs freshness checks; a missing process with no terminal record is an unknown outcome, not success.

Cancellation and cleanup must be ordered: request stop, establish terminal state, preserve diagnostic evidence, then remove only disposable owned artifacts. Remote or inaccessible process state must fail closed. Keep this machinery reusable for standalone validation rather than creating a second job engine.

ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.

applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
